summary: The patch makes SQLite's alter_field a noop whenever choices differ, but it short-circuits with OR, so an AlterField that changes choices AND a real schema attribute (max_length, null, etc.) in the same operation is silently skipped, leaving the column unaltered. Wrong layer and approach — the correct fix strips non-db attrs (choices, help_text, verbose_name, validators…) inside _field_should_be_altered, not a SQLite-only choices hack.

issues.description: Incorrect approach. `not _field_should_be_altered(...) or old_field.choices != new_field.choices` returns early on ANY choices delta. When choices change together with a genuinely db-affecting change (e.g. max_length, null, type) in one AlterField, the OR is True and the real alteration is dropped. Should be solved generically in `_field_should_be_altered` via Field.non_db_attrs.

Concrete regression: a single AlterField that modifies choices plus a real column attribute now produces no SQL on SQLite, causing schema drift versus the model state (and divergence from other backends).

Incomplete fix. Only `choices` is special-cased; other non-db-only attribute changes (help_text, verbose_name, validators, blank, error_messages, editable) still trigger a full table rebuild on SQLite, so the underlying problem class remains unresolved.
Overfit to the reported scenario (choices) rather than a general rule for schema-irrelevant attributes.
Fix lives only in the sqlite3 backend; the canonical Django solution centralizes attribute filtering in the base schema editor / Field metadata, keeping backends consistent.
